meta.authorship_gap: ALL 69 items are builder-authored (mined from MODLOG rulings; B25-B69 added 2026-09-04 covering M72-M195k). Founder-authored items still pending — until they exist, every report from this bank must carry the line 'builder-authored bank'.

scale.1: partially right, or honestly declines to answer without contradicting the required fact
scale.0: contradicts the required fact, or confidently asserts specifics not on the map

items.question: A user ran '/plugin marketplace update harnessmap' and then '/plugin install map@harnessmap' but still has the old plugin version. What exact command gets them the newest version?
items.required_fact: /plugin update map@harnessmap (then restart Claude Code)
items.provenance: real failure: we shipped the wrong instruction and a founder stayed on 0.9.6
items.author: builder

items.question: Should we set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment when running the test suites or the playground server? How is inference billed?
items.required_fact: no — everything runs on the Claude subscription path; any key present is scrubbed at boot so children cannot see it; only explicit HARNESSMAP_INFERENCE=api uses a key
items.provenance: real failure: weeks of calls billed a founder's key
items.author: builder

items.question: When a user switches on 'close map influence' (the ⏻ switch), does the map stop filing what they talk about?
items.required_fact: no — filing continues quietly; only the map's influence on sessions stops (no injections, no mentions), so the map is current when reopened
items.provenance: founder ruling with explicit requirement that filing continues
items.author: builder

items.question: Jacob messaged 'the two mode thing is fine actually'. Earlier there was discussion of a two-mode interface toggle. Should we build the two-mode toggle now?
items.required_fact: no — the two-mode decision was historically misread as approval once, the build was reversed, and the concept was parked; only an explicit founder decision revives it
items.provenance: real failure: 'fine actually' was misread as build authority
items.author: builder

items.question: Should the folders in the pinned band (to sort / favorites / to tidy) be hidden when they are empty?
items.required_fact: no — they stay visible when empty so the mechanism stays discoverable; an earlier hide-when-empty behavior was explicitly reversed
items.author: builder

items.question: When the tidy agent proposes renames for map nodes, how long should proposed names be?
items.required_fact: short: topic/heading nodes about 2-5 words (containers 2-4), statement nodes one tight sentence; never make a name longer without making it clearer
items.author: builder

items.question: When a large import is applied to the map, do the newly created nodes arrive lit or dim?
items.required_fact: dim — an import lands dim and the user chooses focus and may auto-light; born-lit applies to normal per-round filing, not imports
items.provenance: ruling after a 2,169-node import auto-lit the whole map
items.author: builder

items.question: A user asks: 'the map port on my laptop is forwarded to a server on another machine — will my sessions bind to it?'
items.required_fact: no — hooks refuse a server answering from another machine (the server reports its machine name and the hook checks it), telling the user to close or move the tunnel rather than misbinding
wrong_answers: it will bind to whatever answers on the port
items.provenance: real failure: a founder's tunnel nearly filed his conversations onto our playground
items.author: builder

items.question: Can a website the user visits read the map through the localhost port (for example over a WebSocket to localhost:8790)?
items.required_fact: no — on the loopback bind the Host header must be local and any Origin must be local, which blocks cross-origin WebSockets, DNS rebinding, and CSRF; originless clients like hooks and curl still pass
wrong_answers: localhost binding alone makes it safe
items.provenance: security review finding, guard shipped with suite checks
items.author: builder

items.question: What is the map's per-injection size budget, and where does the number come from?
items.required_fact: about 5% of the harness context window — 200k tokens gives roughly 10k tokens ≈ 40k characters — overridable by settings/env; it is derived, not an arbitrary constant
wrong_answers: a fixed arbitrary number with no basis
items.provenance: founder ruling deriving budget from the harness window
items.author: builder

items.question: The chat agent inside the map's own chat pane — does it have tools like web search or file access?
items.required_fact: no tools at all — when the user needs them it says so in one line and points at the ＋ session button, where a real Claude Code session on the same map has tools and inherits the context
items.provenance: founder ruling with inline ＋ session button
items.author: builder

items.question: How often does the automatic map review (auto-tidy proposals) run?
items.required_fact: every 10 filed rounds OR every 30 minutes since the last review, whichever comes first — checked at round completion; an idle map reviews nothing; first review at round 5; propose-only
items.provenance: founder set both the count and the time trigger
items.author: builder

items.question: When the user says hello or makes small talk, what should the chat agent do about the map?
items.required_fact: nothing — greetings and small talk are never map business; reply in kind and stop, no focus offers, no map status, no 'want to get back to X?'
items.provenance: real failure: the agent offered to refocus after 'hello'
items.author: builder

items.question: A topic the user discussed landed in 'to sort'. What are the ways it gets out of there?
items.required_fact: re-light its suggested home (the map moves it next round), ↖ place (agent-suggested homes with browse fallback), ★ promote to top level, mention it in chat, or a tidy — and moves out strip the provenance note
items.author: builder

items.question: Who may restructure the map on its own initiative — the filer, the tidy agent, or neither?
items.required_fact: neither — the filer never restructures (it suggests via dots), and every restructuring (tidy, place, import) is a proposal the user approves; propose-then-approve is standing law
wrong_answers: the filer reorganizes as it files
items.author: builder

items.question: What does the user's lighting control, exactly — reading, writing, or both?
items.required_fact: both, asymmetrically: it bounds what the chat agent sees as background AND where the map agent may write; the map agent may expand its READING on its own once per round (up to 3 branches) but writing outside the light always goes to 'to sort'
items.author: builder

items.question: Are the machine-maintained memory layers of a node (its one-line version, its summary, how-it-fits) editable by the user?
items.required_fact: no — machine-maintained layers are read-only for the user; the user edits only title, description, and category
items.author: builder

items.question: What are the three lengths every node's memory exists at, and what does each contain?
items.required_fact: minimal, medium, and long — and each contains the WHOLE node at that size: minimal is one sentence of everything, medium is up to 150 words of everything, long is every layer in full (statement, dated specifics with links, discussion record)
wrong_answers: lengths that are subsets rather than compressions
items.provenance: founder command, corrected once after being misbuilt
items.author: builder

items.question: When does a topic get served at full length in the agent's briefing even though it sits far from the user's focus?
items.required_fact: when the user's message names it — the question rides into the composition and the named topic is promoted to full for that turn, even from beneath the rolled-up fold; only within lit territory
wrong_answers: the agent decides to look it up on its own (measured: it doesn't)
items.provenance: founder yes; built because agents never pull unprompted (0 of 18)
items.author: builder

items.question: Does closing map influence also block the agent-initiated recall/lookup of map content?
items.required_fact: yes — closed means silent in both directions; recall is refused while influence is closed
items.author: builder

items.question: What happens to a proposal (a big import, a tidy) that the user hasn't applied yet if the server restarts?
items.required_fact: it survives — pending proposals persist to the database and reload on boot; this was ruled after a 588-node import proposal was lost to a restart
items.author: builder

items.question: What model tier do the per-round background agents (filer, memory, naming) run on, and whose account pays?
items.required_fact: the cheap tier through the user's own Claude Code sign-in (subscription path) — no separate API billing unless the user explicitly opts into api mode
items.provenance: founder rulings on tiering and billing
items.author: builder

items.question: A node's name in the map ran long and ugly after a bad model round. What fixes names like this, and when?
items.required_fact: the store rejects titles over 6 words/64 chars, and a healer sweep auto-renames broken display names at boot and after every round — names self-heal without the user asking
items.provenance: founder ruling: broken names always self-heal
items.author: builder

items.question: May the assistant introduce new product vocabulary (new names for concepts) when building or explaining features?
items.required_fact: no — the vocabulary is closed: founders' words are the vocabulary; new concepts reuse existing words or don't ship, and this applies to internal names too
wrong_answers: new coinages are fine if explained
items.provenance: repeated founder corrections in one day
items.author: builder

items.question: The tidy agent is reviewing one subtree. May it read the whole map to decide?
items.required_fact: no — tidy reads only the local neighborhood of its target; whole-map review is tidy-map's own job (a separate root-scope lane)
wrong_answers: tidy always reads the whole map
items.author: builder

items.question: A round was chit-chat that seems irrelevant to the project. Should the tidy agent remove those nodes as irrelevant?
items.required_fact: no — tidy never drops for irrelevance; relevance is focus/light's job, tidy only restructures what exists
items.author: builder

items.question: What kind of map is this product's map — a deliberation map that only records weighing/decisions, or something broader?
items.required_fact: a TOPIC map — whatever gets discussed is a topic and belongs on the map, with no dignity threshold; deliberation structure grows under topics when it exists
items.author: builder

items.question: The user asks to merge two views of the map they were using. What happened to merge-views as a feature?
items.required_fact: merge-views was REMOVED — recency is the chat lifecycle; node, chat, and project merges exist instead
items.author: builder

items.question: Does zooming into a branch change what the chat agent sees?
items.required_fact: no — zoom is view-only and never touches lighting; 'dim all outside' is its own explicit action
items.author: builder

items.question: The user tries to dim a node that lies on the current focus path. What happens?
items.required_fact: refused — the focus path cannot be dimmed while the conversation is aimed through it; move the focus first (cascaded descendants on the path are skipped silently in bulk ops)
items.author: builder

items.question: The user clicks add-node. What name does the new node get and where does the conversation aim?
items.required_fact: it is created unnamed ('untitled') and focused — the first round names it; the system, not the user, supplies the name from what gets discussed
wrong_answers: the user must type a name first
items.author: builder

items.question: When the product's own prompts and UI refer to its background agents, what naming rule applies?
items.required_fact: canonical agent names everywhere — one fixed cast (filer, tidy, auto-light, auto-focus, the reviewer, the map status agent…); no ad-hoc synonyms
items.author: builder

items.question: The expand control on a node shows how much of the subtree?
items.required_fact: only the immediate children — one level per expand
items.author: builder

items.question: How do the map's background agents coordinate — do they talk to each other?
items.required_fact: no agent chat — coordination is one-way: a shared system card, the user's map preferences, and typed requests/referrals; hierarchy, not conversation (M124), and the brain's reports flow down as consults
items.author: builder

items.question: What does the ⌂ home button aim at, and can the user change it?
items.required_fact: home is the whole map by default, always exists, and any node can be set as home from its row — home is a row button
wrong_answers: home is fixed to the root forever
items.author: builder

items.question: A user asks: does closing the map influence stop the map from being mentioned by the agent?
items.required_fact: yes — closed influence means no injections AND no mentions of the map at all, while filing continues quietly in the background
wrong_answers: the agent still mentions the map
items.author: builder

items.question: Where does ALL user data live for an installed harnessmap, and why does that matter for support?
items.required_fact: in ONE place: ~/.harnessmap (db, server log, port file) — overridable by env for dev/playground; support asks start there
items.author: builder

items.question: What is Claude's own memory to the import dialog?
items.required_fact: a first-class import source — the per-project auto-memory files (MEMORY.md + notes) are listed alongside project documents and past sessions
items.provenance: Jacob: directly importing memory from user's Claude
items.author: builder

items.question: How often does auto-tidy review run, and what does HARNESSMAP_AUTOTIDY_ROUNDS=0 do?
items.required_fact: every 10 filed rounds or 30 minutes since the last review (whichever first, checked at round completion; idle maps review nothing); setting the env var to 0 switches the rhythm off — the suites' established off-switch
wrong_answers: it runs on a fixed timer regardless of activity
items.author: builder

items.question: The user greets the agent with 'good morning'. What does the filer produce for that round?
items.required_fact: nothing — pure dialogue mechanics (greetings, thanks, confirmations) are the ONLY rounds that produce no nodes
items.author: builder

items.question: What are the three lengths every node's memory is stored at, and what rule do their contents obey?
items.required_fact: minimal, medium, long — each contains the WHOLE node at that size (one sentence of everything / ≤150 words of everything / every layer), never subsets of different fields
items.author: builder

items.question: How is the per-injection budget spent across lit topics (the resolution rule)?
items.required_fact: by focus proximity: the focus neighborhood serves long, near/recent topics medium, everything else at least its minimal line with a '+N inside' fold at scale — degrading gracefully down that ladder, never truncating arbitrarily
items.author: builder

items.question: A host session's second turn: does it get the full map block again?
items.required_fact: no — full block once (per session and after compaction), then deltas rendered as current-state lines; a fresh full block returns on the 15-change threshold, a refocus, a mass lighting change, ⟲ refresh, or compaction
wrong_answers: the full block is injected every turn
items.author: builder

items.question: What does the ⟲ refresh agent context button do, and is /compact required afterwards?
items.required_fact: every session on the map gets a fresh FULL map view on its next message; /compact in the terminal is optional cleanup of the older map blocks — everything works without it because the fresh view supersedes them
items.provenance: founders' refresh ruling with the wording rule
items.author: builder

items.question: Which surfaces run the governed full-then-delta injection economy after the consolidation?
items.required_fact: both the chat pane and Claude Code sessions — one machinery (pane anchors ride as pane:<chatId>); Codex support is shelved for its own track; influence-off stays a separate mode
items.author: builder

items.question: The user re-aims the map mid-conversation (new focus, relights a branch). What does the next turn's injection carry?
items.required_fact: a fresh FULL map block composed for the new aim (re-aim re-anchors every session on the project), with the notice that /compact is optional
wrong_answers: a one-line delta about the change only
items.author: builder

items.question: The user's question names a topic that is lit but far from focus, on a delta turn. What happens?
items.required_fact: the server's every-turn matcher serves that node in full right in the injection — authorization exists because it is lit; the question no longer waits for a full-block turn
wrong_answers: nothing until the next full block
items.author: builder

items.question: The user's question touches a SET-ASIDE (dim) topic. What exactly reaches the agent?
items.required_fact: a one-line offer naming the topic with a single-use pullupToken — zero content; the agent offers to pull it up, and only the user's yes redeems the token through recall, serving the node once with the lit set untouched
wrong_answers: the content is served since the user asked
items.author: builder

items.question: Can the agent reuse a pull-up token to read the dim node again next turn?
items.required_fact: no — the token is single-use (and expires in minutes); another read needs another offer and another yes
wrong_answers: the token stays valid for the session
items.author: builder

items.question: What is the overall map status report, and who is it for?
items.required_fact: the map status agent's one coherent judgment of the map (essence, arc, tensions, keystones, gaps, trust per area, plus per-job advice) — FOR THE MAP ITSELF: the working agents consult it; the user sees it in 🩺 map status for transparency only
items.author: builder

items.question: Which reporters feed the overall map status report's synthesis?
items.required_fact: structure-status, content-status (chapter assessments for all areas), historical-status (the map's biography from events/aggregates/import records), the user's own edits verbatim as the highest authority, the taste note, the user's standing guidance, and its own previous text
wrong_answers: it reads the raw map directly
items.author: builder

items.question: What do the working agents receive from the overall map status report — the report itself?
items.required_fact: the trimmed report PLUS the brain's actual advice for their specific job (filing/lighting/review/chat), both from the same cycle so they stay coherent; tidy alone stays in its lane with the structural opinion only
wrong_answers: the full report is dumped to every agent
items.author: builder

items.question: Which model tier runs the overall report's synthesis, and why?
items.required_fact: the smartest tier (the import's tier) — the brain is the one judgment everything else consults; its reporters stay on the cheap tier
items.author: builder

items.question: Two duty rules were written into the brain's charter after its first real failures. Name them.
items.required_fact: internal consistency (never trust in one section what you distrust in another) and dates-not-prominence (currency claims stand on dates and statuses, never on how big a node is) — later joined by numbers-before-narrative
items.provenance: learned from the false fork claim and v0.4.1-as-current
items.author: builder

items.question: What must the brain write BEFORE any section of its report, and what must it contain?
items.required_fact: its reconciliation — the minimum work: every input covered by name (accept/reject/partly and why) with the measured numbers quoted; it may never assert an absence the numbers contradict
items.provenance: Jacob: a minimum budget that must be used in full — denominated in obligations
items.author: builder

items.question: How does a large import's proposal begin, before any chunk is filed?
items.required_fact: with a very long comprehensive summary of the whole source (the one-time impression maker, up to ~3,000 words) — every chunk files against it, and it is persisted at apply as the standard the finished map is judged by
wrong_answers: chunks file with only their own slice
items.author: builder

items.question: When does an import count as successful?
items.required_fact: only when the overall map status report, after the import and brain cycle, is judged similar enough to the import's own source summary — mismatches drive mutual revisions until a later verify passes
items.author: builder

items.question: Verification says the finished import doesn't match its source. Whose click fixes it?
items.required_fact: nobody's — the machinery's: map-side findings drive an automatic tidy AND automatic filing from the source summary, inside the imported subtree only, cycle after cycle until the verdict flips; the user approved once, at landing
wrong_answers: the user must approve each fix
items.provenance: Jacob: it's the filer's click not my
items.author: builder

items.question: The automatic finish proposes a node parented OUTSIDE the imported subtree. What happens to that round?
items.required_fact: only the stray re-homes to the import root (per-node mandate, the orphan-sweep precedent) — the round is never refused wholesale; a whole-round escape is refused and audited
items.provenance: found live: two good rounds were thrown away
items.author: builder

items.question: What does find-and-file do, and what authorizes it?
items.required_fact: the applied import's FULL source stays with the map; the user asks in plain words, the source is searched mechanically, and the matches are filed through the same finish machinery into the import's branch — the user's ask is the approval
wrong_answers: the source is discarded after import
items.provenance: Jacob: the user controls the finisher after the import
items.author: builder

items.question: What does ✚ enrich map do, and why is it propose→approve when the import's finish is automatic?
items.required_fact: it reads the map's own conversation record, finds thin nodes discussed at length, and proposes the depth under them — propose→approve because no mandate covers the whole map; the import's one approval covered only its subtree
items.provenance: Jacob's coarse-map ruling with the mandate boundary
items.author: builder

items.question: A proposal was made while project A was active, but project B is active when the user applies it. Where does it land?
items.required_fact: on project A — a proposal applies to the project it was proposed for; the pending row's project stamp wins over the mutable active project
wrong_answers: on whatever project is active at apply
items.provenance: found live: 513 nodes landed on the wrong map
items.author: builder

items.question: How large is a chapter assessment, and what happens when one chapter dominates the map?
items.required_fact: size follows the area (100-150 words for small areas up to ~500 for large ones, reading slice scaled too); a chapter over ~120 nodes or ~40% share is assessed BY ITS PARTS one level down, its own row becoming the roll-up naming them
wrong_answers: a flat 150 words for every chapter
items.author: builder

items.question: Who may talk directly to the map status agent, and what does the exchange leave behind?
items.required_fact: the user, from inside 🩺 map status — the agent answers from its current understanding and the exchange distills into standing guidance (≤200 words, integrated, retractions dropped) that rides every future synthesis, outranked only by the user's edits
items.author: builder

items.question: The brain flags a contradiction that turns out to be false. Why is that poison rather than benign?
items.required_fact: every agent consults the brain, so a false flag steers filing, lighting, and chat wrong everywhere at once — true flags heal, false flags poison; the alarms are the stamps, grounding duties, and the bank
wrong_answers: a wrong flag is harmless advice
items.provenance: the false-tension risk, on the record
items.author: builder

items.question: What is the primary comparison of the recall test, and what is the honest opponent?
items.required_fact: map briefing versus a transcript slice at EQUAL character budget — the transcript slice is what a user's agent has without the product; an empty-context opponent would be a rigged win
items.author: builder

items.question: Why is the bank's target size 69 items?
items.required_fact: computed from measured variance: sd of paired per-item differences 0.92 (90 archived pairs) → 69 items detects a 0.4 difference at α=.05 two-sided with power .95; below that, claims stay exploratory
items.author: builder

items.question: A recall run's grader disagrees with the double-grade check. What does the instrument do?
items.required_fact: below chance-corrected agreement .70 it self-quarantines — the run's numbers are not reported except as quarantined; the rubric gets fixed before rerunning
items.author: builder

items.question: Every recall score in the ledger decomposes into which three classes?
items.required_fact: recalled / served-but-wrong (the serving-selection class, e.g. confident inversions) / never-filed (staleness — the fact isn't on the map at all); each class points at a different fix
items.author: builder
